name: Yahuna
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Tucanoan; only Koch-Grunberg-era wordlists cited on Glottolog, no phonological description found

sources.citation: Anon. 2025. Prácticas lingüísticas, identidades fluidas y exogamia: reflexiones a partir de la historia de los yaunas del río Apaporis. Revista Colombiana de Antropología.
sources.note: Companion sociolinguistic-historical article on the Yauna; may cite any unpublished Yahuna language material.

sources.citation: Eraso, Natalia. 2015. Gramática tanimuka, una lengua de la Amazonía colombiana. PhD thesis, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (531 pp.).
sources.note: Phonology is Tanimuka's, not Yahuna's. On Yahuna only classification/ethnohistory: pp. 16-17 Loukotka grouped yahuna with tanimuca; Koch-Grünberg treated Tanimuka as a Yahuna horde (quoting Ardila); Waltz & Wheeler 1972 left Yahuna unclassified; p. 40 and p. 37 mention the Yahúna/Yauna people. Nothing on Yahuna stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 page for yahu1241 (classification Tucanoan > Eastern > South; alt. names Jaúna, Yauna, Yayuna; AES extinct per Ardila 2010; subclassification refs Chacon 2014 and Ramirez 2019).
sources.note: No descriptive reference listed; Ramirez 2019 (ref 576304) is 'A Fala Tukano dos Ye'pâ-Masa', a Tucano grammar/dictionary, not a Yahuna source.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1915-16. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete (Schluss). Anthropos 10/11: 421-449; pp. 445-449 'Yahúna (Rio Apaporis)', recorded by Rafael Tobar (d. 1912), copied from his manuscript by Hermann Schmidt.
sources.note: Second-hand wordlist and phrases in Spanish-based orthography with almost no accent marks; one footnote (p. 445) on re-transcribing Spanish j; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1914. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete (Fortsetzung). Anthropos 9: 812-832. Comparative wordlist Desána / Yupúa / Yahúna (Rio Apaporis) / Kuerétu.
sources.note: The only primary Yahúna data: ~20 pages of accent-marked wordlist (acute on the stressed vowel per the 1912 key, e.g. tihoképe 'mouth', amoképea 'ear-hole', lupukéa 'head') plus footnotes on consonants and vowels (p. 812 n.1 the l/r/d sound; p. 829 n.3 the dull u/e vowel). No sentence about accent placement.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1913. Betóya-Sprachen.. Anthropos 8: 944-977 (scanned text of the whole volume checked).
sources.note: Only a reprint of the 1912 introduction/Lautlehre (p. 948: '´ Wortakzent'); the single Yahúna mention (p. 948) says Schmidt's Yahúna list was partly copied from a Spanish manuscript and contains numerous grammatical forms. No stress rule.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1912. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete. Anthropos 7: 429-462 (introduction and Lautlehre, pp. 429-434 extracted).
sources.note: Notation key only (p. 433): acute = 'Wortakzent', macron = length; no statement of where the accent falls in any Betóya language. p. 432: the Yahúna list was taken by K-G himself in March-April 1905 on the lower Apaporis; p. 434 remark on Yahúna's l/r/d sound; p. 431: Yahúna 'differs in many ways' from the Uaupés/Pirá-Paraná Betóya dialects, hordes Opaina (Tanimboka-tapuyo), Datuana, Yahúna proper, Kuschiita.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en), 'Yahuna language' (stub); ASJP lexibank list YAHUNA (Bischoffberger, from Koch-Grünberg 1912-16) in the local ASJP copy.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; both point back to Koch-Grünberg.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1909-10. Zwei Jahre unter den Indianern: Reisen in Nordwest-Brasilien 1903/1905, Bd. 2. Berlin: Wasmuth.
sources.note: Ethnographic account of the 1905 stay among the Yahúna on the Apaporis; may contain additional accent-marked Yahúna words or songs, no rule expected.

sources.citation: Ospina-Bozzi, Ana María & Joan Sebastián Gutiérrez Rodríguez. 2025. Gentes y maneras de hablar en el río Apaporis (Colombia): el caso de YAUNA, TANIMUCA y LETUAMA. Tipití 21(1), art. 4.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists at the publisher (DOI recorded); open or paywalled, not checked; the linked copy could not be retrieved
sources.note: Newest treatment of what 'Yauna' denotes linguistically (identity of Koch-Grünberg's Yahúna vs. the present-day Yauna who speak Tanimuka); needed for the identity note rather than for a stress statement.

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago. 2014. A revised proposal of Proto-Tukanoan consonants and Tukanoan family classification. International Journal of American Linguistics 80(3): 275-322.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative-historical; Glottolog cites pp. 5-7 for Yahuna's subgrouping and it may say what Yahuna data (Koch-Grünberg) were used and how the accent marks were interpreted; would not give a first-hand stress rule.

sources.citation: von Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp. 1867. Wörtersammlung Brasilianischer Sprachen (Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. 2). Leipzig: Fleischer.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Listed by Glottolog as an overview source for Yahuna; 19th-century wordlist material only (Koch-Grünberg 1912 p. 431 cites Martius for the Yupúa); no stress statement expected.
